description: Inspect a small commercial building's electrical installation including motor circuits, feeders, load calculations, and equipment disconnects. Verify proper conductor sizing, overcurrent protection, and code compliance for commercial occupancies.
environmentDescription: A small commercial space with multiple motor installations (HVAC compressors, exhaust fans), a mechanical room with subpanel and feeders, a battery/UPS closet, and an office area with general receptacle and lighting circuits.

violations.description: Motor branch circuit overcurrent protection device exceeds Table 430.52 maximum

citations.text: A motor branch circuit's short-circuit and ground-fault device follows the percentages in Table 430.52 and stays at or below the maximum they give.

violations.hintText: Check the breaker size against the motor's full-load current. Table 430.52 sets the maximum OCPD size for different motor types.
violations.inspectionNote: The 50A breaker on this 10HP motor exceeds the maximum allowed by Table 430.52 for an inverse-time breaker (typically 250% of FLC).

violations.description: Motor branch circuit conductors undersized — not 125% of motor full-load current

citations.text: Conductors for one continuously running motor need ampacity of at least 125 percent of its full-load current (taken per 430.6(A)(1)).

violations.hintText: Motor branch circuit conductors must be sized at 125% of the motor's full-load current from Table 430.248/250.
violations.inspectionNote: 10 AWG conductors supply a 7.5HP motor with 22A FLC. Required ampacity is 27.5A (125% of 22A), but 10 AWG is only rated 30A at 60C — marginal with temperature derating applied.

violations.description: Motor disconnect is not within sight of the motor controller

citations.text: A motor disconnect must be in sight of the motor and of the machinery the motor drives.
Install a motor's disconnecting means in sight of the motor and its starter, and within 9 m of them.
citations.hintText: The disconnect must be within sight of the motor and its starter, and within 9 m of them.
citations.inspectionNote: The motor disconnect is located around a corner, out of sight from the motor. The code requires the disconnect to be within sight of the motor and within 9 m of it.

violations.hintText: The disconnect must be within sight from the motor and its controller. 'Within sight' means visible and not more than 50 feet away.
violations.inspectionNote: The motor disconnect is located around a corner, out of sight from the motor. The code requires the disconnect to be within sight of the motor it controls.

violations.description: Motor overload protection exceeds 115% of nameplate full-load amperes

citations.text: A continuous-duty motor over 1 hp needs its own overload device set to trip at no more than 115 percent of nameplate full-load current, or 125 percent when the motor has a service factor of 1.15 or more or a marked temperature rise of 40 C or less.

violations.hintText: Check the overload relay setting against the motor nameplate current. Unless the motor has a service factor of 1.15 or more (or a marked temperature rise of 40 C or less), the maximum is 115% of nameplate FLA.
violations.inspectionNote: The overload relay is set to 30A for a motor with 22A nameplate FLA (136% of FLA). Maximum should be 25.3A (115% of 22A) for a motor with a service factor of 1.0.

violations.description: Calculated service load does not account for all connected loads

citations.text: A feeder or service load must equal at least the sum of the branch-circuit loads it supplies (Part II), after any demand factors allowed by Parts III, IV or V.

violations.hintText: Verify the load schedule accounts for all connected loads: lighting, receptacles, motors, HVAC, and special equipment.
violations.inspectionNote: The load schedule omits the rooftop HVAC unit (15 kVA) from the total service calculation, resulting in an undersized service.

violations.description: Feeder conductor undersized for the calculated load it serves

citations.text: Size feeder conductors to carry the load worked out by the Article 220 calculation methods (its Parts III, IV and V).

violations.hintText: Calculate the total load on this feeder and compare it to the conductor ampacity. Don't forget to add 125% for continuous loads.
violations.inspectionNote: The feeder to the mechanical room subpanel uses 4 AWG copper (85A at 75C) but serves a calculated load of 95A including continuous lighting.

violations.description: Receptacle outlets not calculated at minimum 180 VA per outlet

citations.text: Outside dwelling units, count at least 180 VA for each single or multiple receptacle on one yoke when calculating the load.

violations.hintText: In commercial occupancies, each general-use receptacle outlet must be calculated at a minimum of 180 VA per strap.
violations.inspectionNote: The load calculation uses 90 VA per receptacle instead of the required minimum 180 VA per outlet under the load calculation rules.

violations.description: Equipment grounding conductor undersized for the motor branch circuit OCPD

citations.text: Pick the equipment grounding conductor size from Table 250.122, using the ampere rating or trip setting of the protective device ahead of the circuit.

violations.hintText: The equipment grounding conductor must be sized based on the rating of the overcurrent device, per Table 250.122.
violations.inspectionNote: A 14 AWG EGC is used on a motor circuit protected by a 40A breaker. Table 250.122 requires a minimum 10 AWG copper EGC for a 40A OCPD.

violations.description: Multiple motors on a single branch circuit without proper overcurrent protection sizing

citations.text: For several motors, or a motor plus other loads, conductor ampacity is 125 percent of the largest motor's full-load current plus the full-load currents of the other motors.

violations.hintText: When multiple motors share a feeder, size it at 125% of the largest motor FLC plus 100% of all other motor FLCs.
violations.inspectionNote: The mechanical room feeder supplies three motors but is sized at only 100% of the largest motor plus the sum of the others, missing the required 125% factor on the largest motor.

violations.description: Motor controller disconnect not rated for locked-rotor current

citations.text: A motor circuit's disconnect must be rated at 115 percent or more of the motor's full-load current, and a switch must also suit the motor's horsepower or locked-rotor current.

violations.hintText: The disconnect for a motor controller must be rated to handle the motor's locked-rotor current, not just full-load current.
violations.inspectionNote: The disconnect switch at the VFD is rated for 30A but the motor has a locked-rotor current of 145A. The disconnect must be horsepower-rated or capable of interrupting locked-rotor current.

violations.description: Motor nameplate data missing or illegible

citations.text: Motor nameplates carry the maker, voltage, frequency, phase count, full-load amps, temperature rise or insulation class, ambient temperature, time rating, horsepower and locked-rotor code letter.

violations.hintText: Every motor must have a legible nameplate with all required markings. Can you read the nameplate on this motor?
violations.inspectionNote: The nameplate on this exhaust fan motor is painted over and illegible. Without readable nameplate data, proper conductor sizing and overcurrent protection cannot be verified.

violations.description: Feeder tap conductor does not meet the 10-foot tap rule requirements

citations.text: A feeder tap needs no overcurrent device at the tap if it is no longer than 3.0 m (10 ft), has ampacity of at least the combined calculated loads it serves, and runs in a raceway.

violations.hintText: Feeder taps without overcurrent protection at the tap point must meet strict length, ampacity, and raceway requirements.
violations.inspectionNote: A 12-foot feeder tap is run without overcurrent protection at the tap point and without being enclosed in a raceway. The 10-foot tap rule requires the tap to be no longer than 10 feet and enclosed in a raceway.

violations.description: Service-entrance conductors are much smaller than the rating of the main service disconnect they feed

citations.text: The overcurrent device protecting service conductors must not be rated higher than the ampacity of those service conductors, apart from limited exceptions such as the next-size-up allowance. Separately, 230.42(A) requires the conductors to carry the calculated load.

violations.hintText: Compare the wire size on the service entrance with the ampere rating of the main overcurrent device.
violations.inspectionNote: The main {term:service-disconnect} has a 200 A overcurrent device, but the service conductors are 3 AWG copper, 100 A at the 75 C column. A device rated far above the conductor ampacity leaves the wire unprotected.

violations.description: 12 AWG aluminum conductors protected by a 20 A breaker, more than the limit for that small aluminum size

citations.text: Small aluminum conductors have lower overcurrent limits than copper: 12 AWG aluminum or copper-clad aluminum tops out at 15 A, and 10 AWG at 25 A, after any ambient and bundling corrections.

violations.hintText: Look at the metal marked on the cable jacket, then match the {term:breaker} rating to the conductor size.
violations.inspectionNote: The cable to a rooftop condenser receptacle is marked 12 AWG AL and lands on a 20 A {term:breaker}. Copper at that size would be fine on 20 A, aluminum is not.

violations.description: Ten current-carrying 12 AWG conductors share one conduit with no ampacity derating, yet sit on a 20 A breaker

citations.text: When more than three current-carrying conductors share a raceway or cable for more than 24 in., start from the 90 C column of Table 310.16 and apply the adjustment factor (80% for 4-6, 70% for 7-9, 50% for 10-20). The overcurrent limits in 240.4(D) are then applied to the adjusted ampacity.

violations.hintText: Count the conductors that carry current inside the conduit before you trust the wire size.
violations.inspectionNote: A mechanical-room EMT run longer than 24 in. holds five 2-wire 120 V receptacle circuits, ten 12 AWG THHN current-carrying conductors, each on a 20 A {term:breaker}. At the 50% factor, 30 A (90 C column) becomes 15 A, so the conductors cannot support 20 A, and the round-up allowance in 240.4(B) is not available on receptacle circuits.

violations.description: A continuous 48 A EV charger is wired with 8 AWG copper, which is not large enough once the 125% factor is applied

citations.text: For a branch circuit with continuous loads (running three hours or more), conductors need ampacity of at least 125% of that continuous load plus 100% of any non-continuous load.

violations.hintText: The nameplate says how long this load runs. Multiply it before comparing with the wire's ampacity.
violations.inspectionNote: A 48 A continuous EV charger (nameplate) sits on a 60 A {term:breaker} with 8 AWG copper THHN (50 A at 75 C). 48 x 1.25 = 60 A, so 6 AWG (65 A at 75 C) is needed; the 60 A {term:breaker} looks right, which hides the problem.

violations.description: A sub-panel feeder is made from two small 2 AWG conductors per phase connected in parallel

citations.text: Phase and neutral conductors may be paralleled only when each is 1/0 AWG or larger. Smaller conductors cannot be joined at both ends to make up a larger circuit.

violations.hintText: Look at the feeder to the sub-panel: how many conductors land on each terminal, and how large is each?
violations.inspectionNote: Each phase lug of the sub-panel feeder holds two 2 AWG copper conductors tied together. Paralleled sets must start at 1/0 AWG, so the feeder should be a single larger conductor per phase.

violations.description: 8 AWG conductors supply a 45 A load but land on equipment terminals marked for 60 C only

citations.text: For circuits of 100 A or less, ampacity cannot exceed the 60 C column unless the terminals are listed and marked for higher-rated conductors. Insulation rating alone does not override the terminal limit.

violations.hintText: Read the label next to the lugs on the equipment, not only the wire insulation printing.
violations.inspectionNote: 8 AWG THHN (rated 90 C) feeds a 45 A heater, but the heater's terminal label says 60 C. The 60 C column gives 40 A for 8 AWG, less than the 45 A load.

violations.description: Rooftop conduit sits on the roof surface in direct sun, with conductors sized without the sunlight temperature adder

citations.text: Where raceways or cables sit in direct sunlight on or above a roof with the bottom less than 3/4 in. above the roof (7/8 in. in earlier editions), add 33 C (60 F) to the outdoor temperature before using the ambient correction table.

violations.hintText: Measure how far the bottom of the conduit is from the roof, then think about what sun does to the air inside it.
violations.inspectionNote: A conduit with 8 AWG THHN to a 50 A rooftop unit rests about 0.5 in above the roof. With the 33 C adder, a 35 C summer day becomes 68 C, giving a 0.58 factor, and the conductors cannot support 50 A.

sceneFact.note: from roof surface to the bottom of the conduit

compliantFact.note: from roof surface to the bottom of the conduit

violations.description: A sub-panel feeder of 4 AWG aluminum serves an 80 A load; it was sized from the copper column, not the aluminum one

citations.text: Ampacity comes from the table column for the conductor material and temperature rating. Aluminum carries less current than copper of the same size, so copper values cannot be used for aluminum conductors.

violations.hintText: Check the feeder's material marking against the load it serves.
violations.inspectionNote: The feeder tag reads 4 AWG aluminum and the sub-panel schedule shows an 80 A load on an 80 A breaker. A 4 AWG copper conductor would carry about 85 A, but 4 AWG aluminum carries only about 65 A at the 75 C column.

violations.description: A 4-wire feeder serving LED and computer loads has 1/0 AWG copper conductors sized without counting the neutral as current-carrying

citations.text: On a 4-wire three-phase wye circuit where most of the load is nonlinear, the neutral carries harmonic current and counts as a current-carrying conductor when applying the adjustment factors for bundled conductors.

violations.hintText: Count the conductors in the conduit, then think about what kind of loads the neutral carries.
violations.inspectionNote: A conduit holds three phase conductors and a neutral of 1/0 AWG THHN copper feeding a panel labelled for servers and LED drivers, with a 140 A load per phase. Counting the neutral gives four conductors and an 80 percent factor, about 136 A, which is below the load.
